decisions.reason: A complete same-message MODIFY already records that the layout and CAD must accommodate the approved, larger 3000 RPM motors.
A complete same-message MODIFY already replaces the 1500 RPM constraint with the approved adjustable 3000 RPM motor selection and removes the obsolete constraint key.
A complete same-message MODIFY already records the 3000 RPM maximum, adjustable range, and approved slow-mixing and higher-speed-frothing modes.
The same-message INTRODUCE already records the operational constraint against constant maximum-speed use and the accepted prolonged-use expectation.
A complete same-message MODIFY already records controlled splashing at higher speeds and the acceptable mitigation options.
Approval of the 3000 RPM motor and adjustable speed range does not change the existing solenoid-based dispensing behavior.
The motor approval does not alter the existing strategy of using off-the-shelf electrical components for the first prototype.
The source addresses speed control, splash control, and smooth mixing but does not change the unit's structural stability or vibration-control requirements.
The approved motor speed does not modify the existing requirement to prevent liquid from reaching electrical components.
A complete same-message MODIFY already records that mixing must remain smooth rather than overly aggressive at higher speeds.
The source approves motor speed and control behavior but does not change the prototype's standard 120V wall-power source.
The source does not modify the existing bowl or spout sealing requirements; its cleanliness concern is specifically about controlling splash during higher-speed mixing.
